questions.question: Which of these is not acceptable emergency equipment?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four yellow squares
questions.explanation: You must show emergency equipment during a vehicle inspection. Acceptable equipment includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or six fuses or three liquid burning flares, and a working fire extinguisher.

questions.question: How should carry-on baggage be stored?

options.text: May be left in the aisle
Must be stored away from the aisle
Must be kept on the rider's lap
Should be placed in the aisle

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be stored away from the aisle
questions.explanation: Baggage must never be left in the aisle or doorway. All luggage must be stored so riders can exit through any window or door in an emergency.

questions.question: What is the best way to check your lights during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Park near a mirror to see the reflection
Turn on the lights, then get out and look at them
Check the instrument panel for warning lights
Drive in traffic and wait for other drivers to signal if lights are out

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the lights, then get out and look at them
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, turn on your lights and then exit the vehicle to look at them.

questions.question: A person working on a disabled vehicle on the road shoulder:

options.text: Will likely pay attention to traffic
May be focused on the repair and not watching traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: May be focused on the repair and not watching traffic
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people repairing disabled vehicles. They may be focused on the repair and not aware of traffic or other hazards.

questions.question: If federal inspectors say your vehicle is unsafe, they can:

options.text: Take your vehicle to a garage for repairs
Formally ask you to fix your vehicle's problems
Remove your vehicle from service until it is fixed

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove your vehicle from service until it is fixed
questions.explanation: If a federal or state inspector finds a vehicle unsafe, they can remove it from service until the problems are fixed.

questions.question: During an inspection, brake pads should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Free of oil or grease
questions.explanation: Brake pads and shoes must not have oil, grease, or brake fluid on them.

questions.question: To warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down, you can:

options.text: Lightly tap the brakes a few times before slowing
Turn on one set of turn signals
Put your hand out the window and wave

questions.correctAnswerText: Lightly tap the brakes a few times before slowing
questions.explanation: Before slowing down, lightly tap your brake pedal a few times. This flashes your brake lights and warns drivers behind you.

questions.question: Buses may carry:

options.text: Explosives other than small arms ammunition

questions.correctAnswerText: Small arms ammunition
questions.explanation: Buses can carry small arms ammunition labeled ORM-D, emergency hospital supplies, and drugs. Most other hazardous materials cannot be transported by bus.

questions.question: If confronted by an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver

questions.correctAnswerText: Ignore the driver's gestures
questions.explanation: If confronted by an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Do not make eye contact, do not speed up to challenge them, and do not react to angry gestures.

questions.question: When driving a school bus, your four-way flashers should:

options.text: Be turned on before crossing railroad tracks
Only be used after crossing railroad tracks
Only be used near railroad tracks if a train is approaching

questions.correctAnswerText: Be turned on before crossing railroad tracks
questions.explanation: When driving a school bus, turn on your four-way flashers when approaching and crossing a railroad crossing. Turn them off once your entire vehicle has cleared the tracks.

questions.question: When should a bus be refueled?

options.text: While passengers are on board only if necessary.
While passengers are on board if they agree.

questions.correctAnswerText: While passengers are on board only if necessary.
questions.explanation: Do not refuel a bus when passengers are on board unless it is necessary. Never refuel a bus with passengers inside a closed building.

questions.question: What are multi-speed axles and auxiliary transmissions used for?

options.text: To make a vehicle run more smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: To provide extra gears.
questions.explanation: Multi-speed rear axles and auxiliary transmissions provide extra gears. A selector knob on the gearshift lever controls them.

questions.question: How should the exhaust system be when you check it?
questions.correctAnswerText: Fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Check that no parts of the exhaust system are loose, broken, or missing.

questions.question: Who is responsible for inspecting a vehicle's cargo?

options.text: The owner of the trucking company.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver.
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for inspecting the cargo. The driver must check that the cargo is not overloaded or poorly balanced, is properly secured, does not block the view, and does not block access to emergency equipment.

questions.question: What does a high center of gravity do?

options.text: Makes a vehicle more likely to tip over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes a vehicle more likely to tip over.
questions.explanation: A high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip over.

questions.question: What should you check about the landing gear during a vehicle inspection?

options.text: That it is more worn on one side than the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: That it is fully raised.
questions.explanation: Make sure the landing gear has no missing parts and is fully raised. The crank handle should be secure and the support frame should not be damaged.

questions.question: When inspecting the exhaust system, which should NOT be a concern?

options.text: Exhaust system parts not touching fuel system parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust system parts not touching fuel system parts.
questions.explanation: When inspecting the exhaust system, watch for loose, broken, or missing pipes, mufflers, tailpipes, or stacks; loose or broken mounting brackets, clamps, bolts, or nuts; exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts, tires, or other vehicle parts; and leaking exhaust parts.

questions.question: If a tire fails while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Stay off the brakes and let the vehicle slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes and let the vehicle slow down.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly. Do not use the brakes and let the vehicle slow down on its own. Once the vehicle has slowed down, brake gently, pull off the road, and stop.

questions.question: When must a school bus be evacuated?

options.text: When the bus stalls in winter weather.
When there is danger of a collision.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is danger of a collision.
questions.explanation: Students should usually stay on a school bus during emergencies. Evacuate when the bus stalls on railroad tracks, is on fire, there is a fire risk, there is a hazardous materials spill, or there is danger of a collision.

questions.question: When should you turn off a retarder?
questions.correctAnswerText: When roads are slippery.
questions.explanation: A retarder helps slow a vehicle and reduces brake use. However, it can cause wheels to skid on slippery surfaces. Turn off retarders when roads are wet, snowy, or icy.
